name: Carbon
occurrence: Free as graphite, diamond, and coal; combined in every organic compound, carbonate rock, and atmospheric CO₂.
biologicalRelevance: The backbone element of every biomolecule you're made of — DNA, proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids all build on carbon's ability to form four stable bonds.
notableCharacteristics: Its four valence electrons and small size let it catenate (bond to itself) into chains, rings, and sheets longer than any other element — the entire basis of organic chemistry.
whyHere: Four valence electrons in a small second-shell atom means four strong, directional covalent bonds — enough versatility to build straight chains, branched chains, rings, and sheets, which no other element does at this scale.
didYouKnow: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon, but diamond's rigid 3-D bonding makes it the hardest natural material while graphite's flat sheets slide past each other, making it soft enough to write with.
genZNote: Four bonding slots and somehow built all of organic chemistry with them. Absolute main-character energy, comes in diamond and pencil-lead flavors.
